content.user_title: Add Valid Schema Markup to Web Pages
content.value_statement: Search engines need structured data that matches visible page content. This skill guides JSON-LD schema selection, implementation, validation, and troubleshooting.
actual_capabilities: Selects schema.org types for organization, product, article, FAQ, event, and local business pages.
Defines required and recommended fields for common rich result formats.
Provides JSON-LD implementation patterns for static sites, React, Next.js, CMS, and WordPress.
Explains how to validate markup with rich result and schema validation tools.
Identifies common schema errors, including missing fields and mismatched page content.
Suggests questions to gather page type, goal, data, existing schema, and tech stack details.
limitations: It does not guarantee rich results because search engines make final display decisions.
It does not automatically inspect live pages unless the host agent has separate browsing tools.
It depends on accurate page content and business data from the user.
It does not replace current Google policy review for sensitive or regulated markup.

use_cases.title: Launch Product Schema
use_cases.description: Create product structured data with offers, availability, ratings, and visible page details.

use_cases.title: Improve Article Eligibility
use_cases.description: Map blog or news content to article markup with author, image, publisher, and dates.

use_cases.title: Fix Validation Errors
use_cases.description: Review structured data issues and prepare updates for testing in validation tools.

prompt_templates.title: Choose Schema Type
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner schema planning for one page.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this page description and recommend the best schema.org type. Explain required fields and any rich result limits.

prompt_templates.title: Draft Page Markup
prompt_templates.scenario: Create initial JSON-LD from supplied page data.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create JSON-LD schema for this page using only the visible content and data I provide. Include placement and validation notes.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Existing Markup
prompt_templates.scenario: Find problems in current structured data.
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this existing schema markup against the visible page content. List missing fields, mismatches, warnings, and recommended fixes.

prompt_templates.title: Design Multi-Type Schema
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced implementation for a page with several entities.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a connected schema graph for this page. Include entity relationships, stable identifiers, implementation placement, and a testing checklist.

output_examples.input: A SaaS pricing page needs structured data for the main product and company.
output: Required fields include name, offers, application category, URL, and publisher details.
Validation notes cover visible price matching, stable URLs, and rich result eligibility limits.

output_examples.input: A blog article has errors for missing publisher logo and date modified.
output: The audit identifies missing publisher logo data and recommends adding date modified when the article changes.
It also checks headline, image, author, description, and main page identity fields.
The response includes a testing checklist for rich result and schema validation tools.

output_examples.input: A local business page needs stronger eligibility for local search features.
output: The plan recommends LocalBusiness markup with name, address, telephone, hours, image, and geographic details.
It warns against adding reviews or ratings that are not visible on the page.

best_practices: Match every schema field to visible or authoritative page content.
Use JSON-LD and validate changes before publishing them.
Keep markup updated when prices, dates, ratings, hours, or page content change.
anti_patterns: Do not mark up content that users cannot see on the page.
Do not add self-serving reviews or ratings that violate search guidelines.
Do not copy generic examples without replacing placeholder data with real page data.

faq.question: What does this skill help create?
faq.answer: It helps create and review JSON-LD schema markup for common SEO rich result types.

faq.question: Does it guarantee rich snippets?
faq.answer: No. It improves eligibility, but search engines decide whether to show rich results.

faq.question: Can it fix existing schema errors?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide the current markup and page details so it can identify mismatches and missing fields.

faq.question: Which schema types are covered?
faq.answer: It covers Organization, WebSite, Article, Product, SoftwareApplication, FAQPage, HowTo, BreadcrumbList, LocalBusiness, Review, and Event.

faq.question: What information should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide the page type, visible content, business data, target rich result, existing schema, and implementation platform.

faq.question: Can Claude Code or Codex use this skill?
faq.answer: Yes. The metadata lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.
